chapters.subject: Mathematics – Geometry
chapters.textbookRef: Mathematics Part II – Standard X (Balbharati) • Chapter 1: Similarity
chapters.overview: Master ratio of areas of two triangles, Basic Proportionality Theorem (BPT), Angle Bisector Theorem, AAA/SAS/SSS similarity tests, and ratio of areas of similar triangles across Practice Sets 1.1 to 1.4.
keyPoints: Area ratio of two triangles = (b₁ × h₁) / (b₂ × h₂).
Basic Proportionality Theorem (BPT): A line parallel to one side of a triangle divides the other two sides in the same ratio (AP/PB = AQ/QC).
Angle Bisector Theorem: The ray bisecting an angle divides the opposite side in the ratio of the remaining two sides.
Theorem of Areas of Similar Triangles: If ΔABC ~ ΔPQR, then A(ΔABC)/A(ΔPQR) = AB²/PQ² = BC²/QR² = AC²/PR².
formulasAndRules: Equal Heights: A₁/A₂ = b₁/b₂ | Equal Bases: A₁/A₂ = h₁/h₂
BPT: Line PQ || BC ⇒ AP/PB = AQ/QC
Similar Triangles Areas: A(ΔABC)/A(ΔPQR) = (Corresponding Side Ratio)²

solvedExamples.prompt: Base of a triangle is 9 and height is 5. Base of another triangle is 10 and height is 6. Find the ratio of areas of these triangles.

textbookExerciseSolutions.question: In ΔMNP, NQ is a bisector of ∠N. If MN = 5, PN = 7, MQ = 2.5, then find QP.
textbookExerciseSolutions.conceptUsed: Property of Angle Bisector of a Triangle
textbookExerciseSolutions.stepByStepExplanation: By Angle Bisector property: MN/NP = MQ/QP ⇒ 5/7 = 2.5/QP ⇒ QP = (2.5 × 7)/5 = 0.5 × 7 = 3.5.

textbookExerciseSolutions.question:
Q1: Ratio of corresponding sides of similar triangles is 3 : 5; find ratio of their areas.
Q2: If ΔABC ~ ΔPQR and AB : PQ = 2 : 3, fill in: A(ΔABC)/A(ΔPQR) = ___/___.
textbookExerciseSolutions.conceptUsed: Theorem on Areas of Similar Triangles

classNotebookExercises.prompt: Find ratio of areas if bases are 6 cm, 9 cm and heights are equal.
State the Basic Proportionality Theorem (Thales Theorem).
classNotebookExercises.modelAnswer: If a line parallel to a side of a triangle intersects the remaining sides in two distinct points, then the line divides the sides in the same proportion.

classNotebookExercises.prompt: In ΔABC, DE || BC, AD = 1.8 cm, DB = 5.4 cm, EC = 7.2 cm. Find AE.
In ΔPQR, PM=15, PQ=25, PR=20, NR=8. Is NM || RQ?
classNotebookExercises.modelAnswer: MQ=10 ⇒ PM/MQ=15/10=3/2; PN=12 ⇒ PN/NR=12/8=3/2 ⇒ Equal ratios ⇒ Yes, NM || RQ by Converse of BPT.

classNotebookExercises.prompt: Lines l || m || n cut two transversals with segments AB=12, BC=x, DE=8, EF=4. Find x.
Name the three tests for similarity of two triangles.
classNotebookExercises.modelAnswer: 1) AA (or AAA) Test, 2) SAS Test, 3) SSS Test.

classNotebookExercises.prompt: A 4 m pole casts a 6 m shadow. At the same time a tower casts a 12 m shadow. Find height of tower.
classNotebookExercises.writingGuidance: Use AA similarity of sun-ray right triangles.

classNotebookExercises.prompt: ΔABC ~ ΔPQR, A(ΔABC)=80, A(ΔPQR)=125, AB=4. Find PQ.
classNotebookExercises.writingGuidance: Take square root of simplified area ratio.

classNotebookExercises.prompt: In trapezium ABCD, AB || DC, diagonals meet at O. If AB=20, DC=6, OB=15, find OD.
classNotebookExercises.writingGuidance: Prove ΔOAB ~ ΔOCD by AA test.

classNotebookExercises.prompt: How do congruent triangles differ from similar triangles?
classNotebookExercises.modelAnswer: Similar triangles have the same shape (proportional sides, equal angles), whereas congruent triangles have both the same shape and exact same size.

revisionChecklist: Match vertex order accurately when writing ~ similarity.
Remember area ratio squares the side ratio.

chapters.subject: Mathematics – Geometry
chapters.textbookRef: Mathematics Part II – Standard X (Balbharati) • Chapter 2: Pythagoras Theorem
chapters.overview: Prove and apply Pythagoras Theorem, Geometric Mean Theorem, 30°-60°-90° and 45°-45°-90° triangle rules, Pythagorean triplets, and Apollonius Theorem.
keyPoints: Pythagoras Theorem: In a right triangle, Hypotenuse² = Base² + Height².
Geometric Mean Theorem: If BD ⊥ AC in right ΔABC, then BD² = AD × DC.
Apollonius Theorem: In ΔABC, if M is midpoint of BC, AB² + AC² = 2AM² + 2BM².

solvedExamples.prompt: Find the diagonal of a rectangle whose length is 35 cm and breadth is 12 cm.

textbookExerciseSolutions.question:
Q1: Identify Pythagorean triplets: (1) (3, 5, 4)  (2) (4, 9, 12)  (3) (5, 12, 13)
Q2: In right ΔMNP, ∠MNP = 90°, NQ ⊥ MP, MQ = 9, QP = 4. Find NQ.
textbookExerciseSolutions.formulaExplained: Largest² = sum of squares of other two; NQ² = MQ × QP.
textbookExerciseSolutions.answer: Q1: (1) Yes, (2) No, (3) Yes  |  Q2: NQ = 6

classNotebookExercises.modelAnswer: In a triangle, if the square of one side equals the sum of squares of the remaining two sides, the angle opposite the first side is a right angle (90°).

chapters.subject: Mathematics – Geometry
chapters.textbookRef: Mathematics Part II – Standard X (Balbharati) • Chapter 6: Trigonometry
chapters.overview: Prove trigonometric identities (sin²θ+cos²θ=1, 1+tan²θ=sec²θ, 1+cot²θ=cosec²θ) and solve height-and-distance word problems across Practice Sets 6.1 and 6.2.
keyPoints: Fundamental Identities: sin²θ + cos²θ = 1 | 1 + tan²θ = sec²θ | 1 + cot²θ = cosec²θ.
Reciprocal Relations: cosecθ = 1/sinθ, secθ = 1/cosθ, cotθ = 1/tanθ = cosθ/sinθ.
Angle of Elevation (looking upward from horizontal) vs Angle of Depression (looking downward).

solvedExamples.prompt: If sinθ = 7/25, find cosθ and tanθ.

textbookExerciseSolutions.question:
Q1: If sinθ = 7/25, find cosθ and tanθ.
Q6(1): Prove that (sin²θ / cosθ) + cosθ = secθ.
textbookExerciseSolutions.answer: Q1: cosθ = 24/25, tanθ = 7/24  |  Q6(1): LHS = secθ = RHS (Proved)

textbookExerciseSolutions.question: A person is standing at a distance of 80 m from a church looking at its top. The angle of elevation is 45°. Find the height of the church.
textbookExerciseSolutions.stepByStepExplanation: Let church height = h, distance = 80 m. tan 45° = h/80 ⇒ 1 = h/80 ⇒ h = 80 m.

classNotebookExercises.prompt: Write the three fundamental trigonometric identities.
Write sin, cos, tan values for 0°, 30°, 45°, 60°, 90°.
classNotebookExercises.modelAnswer: sin: 0, 1/2, 1/√2, √3/2, 1; cos: reverse; tan: 0, 1/√3, 1, √3, Not Defined.

classNotebookExercises.prompt: If tanθ = 3/4, find secθ and cosθ.
Prove: sec²θ + cosec²θ = sec²θ × cosec²θ.
Prove: √[(1 − sinθ)/(1 + sinθ)] = secθ − tanθ.
If x = r cosθ and y = r sinθ, find x² + y².
From top of 90 m lighthouse, angle of depression of a ship is 60°. Find distance of ship from lighthouse (√3 = 1.73).
A kite flies at height 60 m with string inclined at 60° to horizontal. Find string length (√3 = 1.73).
Evaluate: 2 tan 45° + cos 30° − sin 60°.
Draw and label Angle of Elevation vs Angle of Depression.
classNotebookExercises.writingGuidance: Both are measured from the horizontal line of sight.
classNotebookExercises.modelAnswer: Elevation goes upward from horizontal; Depression goes downward from horizontal.

revisionChecklist: Convert complex proofs into sinθ and cosθ when stuck.
